newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-KEITH BYARS, SUPER BOWL SPECTATOR NO MORE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-KEITH BYARS, SUPER BOWL SPECTATOR NO MORE.

text.p: Nearly a decade ago, veteran fullback Keith Byars vowed never to go to another Super Bowl unless he was playing in it. He's going on Sunday.

After a career filled with unsatisfying, premature endings to his NFL seasons with Philadelphia and Miami, Byars will line up for the New England Patriots against the Green Bay Packers in Super Bowl XXXI.

"I'd been to a couple of Super Bowls and had a nice time," said Byars, who signed with the Patriots this season after being cut by the Dolphins. "But in the pit of my stomach, I still had a bad taste in my mouth that I wasn't playing in it."
One of the best in the NFL at catching the ball out of the backfield, Byars jumped at the chance to play for Bill Parcells in New England after Miami cut him loose in October.
Byars became an important part of the Patriots offensive scheme when regular fullback Sam Gash was injured in December.
Byars, then a rookie, attended his first Super Bowl in 1986 because his former Ohio State roommate, Pepper Johnson, was playing for the New York Giants.
"I had to go see him play in it," Byars recalled.

The next year, when it was the Washington Redskins' turn to thump the Broncos, Byars went because "Doug Williams was in it, the first black quarterback to start in the Super Bowl. I had to go support him," explained Byars, a self-proclaimed history buff.
"But since that time, I haven't been back. I made up my mind I wasn't ever coming back until I play.
"Now I don't have to answer that question anymore ... I'm in it," he said.
Byars is one of three former Eagles teammates, each with more than 10 years in the league, who have crossed over to the Super Bowl promised land for the first time this year.
Future Hall of Fame defensive end Reggie White and tight end Keith Jackson will be playing for Green Bay.
The three remain very close, although Byars said he has steered clear of his former teammates this week.
"Sunday night, whenever the game is over we're going to be as tight as we ever were," he said.
The Patriots may be 14-point underdogs, but Byars had his dream scenario for the reunion all worked out.
"We're gonna talk about the whole experience and hopefully I'll be consoling them, saying 'your time will come.' I don't want to hear that speech from them," he chuckled.
Either way, it will be better than the sorry post-Super Bowl ritual Byars and White used to engage in.

The two were bitterly disappointed when the Parcells-coached Giants won a second Super Bowl after the 1990 season, convinced their Eagles were a better team -- especially after they beat the Giants in the regular season.
"We beat them pretty good ... and then we lost in the first round of the playoffs ... and the Giants go on to win the Super Bowl," Byars recalled.

He said he and White would call each other after each Super Bowl, saying, "'Man, can you believe who won it this year? We beat this team. That should have been us.' We had that Super Bowl ritual going for a few years," Byars said.
White has jokingly blamed Parcells for stealing his shot at a Super Bowl ring. Ironically, Parcells could do it to White again this year -- as coach of Byars's team.
Byars is thrilled to be playing for the Eagles' old nemesis in Parcells, whose Super Bowl experience could be just the thing to help the Patriots overcome Green Bay.

"The man definitely knows what he's doing," Byars said. "I've always admired him from the outside for his success and had the utmost respect for him. Now, being on the inside ... I can see why he won two Super Bowls, why he beat us.
"He does the little things well and the big things well."
Byars gives Parcells much of the credit for taking a team with so many young players all the way to the ultimate game.
"He knows what to say to a player at the right time, whether he needs to give you a kind word ... or a swift kick in the behind. He has the perfect mixture of the two," Byars said.
While many of the players on both teams this week have appeared somewhat anxious to get on with the game, Byars has been soaking up the two-week long, over-the-top Super Bowl scene.
"The Super Bowl is special and should be special," he said. "I want to sit back and relax and reflect a little bit on the season. And don't forget about the big task at hand."
